What degraded

  • The deck shipped at the round cap at 6.854, under the 8.0 top rung. The art median is 6.6; all three final judges named frames 2 (a lit grey floor) and 6 (the exploded parts as primitives).
  • Two final judges read the cover's 'with no server' and frame 4's 'No server in the loop' as looser than the release, whose c10 describes central server software and a second model. Past the cap only a hard fail may be repaired; neither judge filed one. The web edition carries c10 in full.
  • 28 of 77 due record items stayed unreachable behind the crawl boundary or a host that did not answer and were not re-stamped.
  • tx-2026-0141 and tx-2026-0167 record the same UT San Antonio release; both stay for a maintainer to merge.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it UT San Antonio's flood sensor runs its AI on the device, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

A low-water crossing in San Antonio.

UT San Antonio's September 28th release says flood risk there often climbs block by block before regional alerts sound.

Chen Pan's team built a prototype that judges that risk on the device itself. Four optical water-level sensors at varying heights sit on one solar powered node. TinyML on its microcontroller judges imminent flood risk with no central server. Parts for one prototype run roughly $150 to $220.

A real flood would be the test. The release reports 98.82% validation accuracy in initial assessments after training. It names no site, no city or county running it and no false alarm or missed event figure. The team aims the design at small coastal towns.

The release holds a validation score and a parts cost. Where is the record of the node in a real flood?

#SanAntonio #UTSA #TinyML

The machine changed itself

  • The weekly pass rebuilt the kit Hereford at no. 49's named fix: a head that lowers to the bunk or to graze, a finer mesh for close crops, and one clean topline instead of a doubled back (d92fd2d8).
    Largest object unmodelled (6 runs, 17 rounds) and primitive models (6 runs, 16 rounds).
  • The feed bunk no. 49 built by hand is now a kit model, weathered the way the judges asked, with manure splash up the wall, a worn lip and feed residue in the throat (073890f4).
    No. 49's hero was a clean pale slab; the next feedyard deck starts from a worn one.
  • Fixed a kit bug: a named shirt colour was ignored on 15 of 120 seeds for the kit person (3ac366c2).
    Part of the queued mannequin item.
  • Needs a maintainer: the accent and GRID checks in layout_check have pushed four decks into flat-paint or decal art. The fix is for the engine to report which pixels belong to each object (UPGRADE_BACKLOG 2026-10-12 item 4).
    The engine and render.py are human lane.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

Carousel no. 50 is UT San Antonio's prototype flood warning node, a solar powered post that judges flood risk on its own microcontroller. The deck is a San Antonio low-water crossing on a wet night, with the node as the hero on eight frames and beacon amber lit only where the water has reached a sensor. It ships at the round cap at 6.854 (judges 6.88, 7.222, 6.80), under the 8.0 top rung. What moved it: the first art review called the first rain a screen, so it now falls only where a lamp catches it. Pixel review ran three rounds and flow review two; the flow critic reordered the deck so the radar finding is the stake on frame 2 and the 98.82% score turns the deck on 7 straight into what the release leaves out on 8. The panel found two hard fails, both in the first comment's date (the ordinal, then the year), both repaired. Integrity repairs from the judges: the cover says "on the device" because the release never describes a post; slide 3 says PRECIPITATION, c2's word; slide 2 leads with UT San Antonio's own stake; slides 8 and 9 say drawn to illustrate; slide 6 names the Texas Coastal Management Program grant; slide 8 and the caption name the release's target, small coastal towns. Named and not repaired at the cap: two final judges read "with no server" on the cover and frame 4 as looser than the release, which describes a central site with server software and a larger model (c10). The web edition carries c10. Frames 2 and 6 are the art's weakest. The record: 49 of 77 due items re-stamped, 28 unreachable. tx-2026-0214 admitted (cab beacons instead of warning triangles for automated trucks). The flood sensor release is dated September 28th on both of its record items, which are duplicates left for a maintainer to merge. Caption close: the caption ledger refused a repeat of yesterday's closing question, so the close now asks where the field record is.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
